source_quote: Initial request for the first three months of noninvasive home ventilator use for restrictive thoracic disorders, all of the following:4,5,9 1. Documentation of a neuromuscular disease (ex. amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) or a severe thoracic cage abnormality (ex. post-thoracoplasty for tuberculosis or severe kyphoscoliosis)
clinical_service_or_procedure: Noninvasive Home Ventilator - Restrictive Thoracic Disorders (HCPCS E0466)

criteria.description: Neuromuscular disease (ALS) or severe thoracic cage abnormality
Awake PaCO2 ≥ 45 mm Hg, sleep O2 sat ≤ 88% for ≥5 min, MIP < 60 cm H2O, or FVC < 50%
Cannot be treated with RAD; ventilator will provide AVAPS not CPAP

required_documentation: ABG report documenting PaCO2 ≥ 45 mm Hg or sleep oximetry
Documentation explaining why RAD is inadequate
review_notes: Initial authorization strictly limited to first 3 months.

source_quote: Initial request for the first three months of noninvasive home ventilator use for severe COPD, all of the following: 1. An arterial blood gas PaCO2 measurement was done while awake and breathing at baseline and prescribed FIO2 is ≥ 52 mm Hg;4
clinical_service_or_procedure: Noninvasive Home Ventilator - Severe COPD (HCPCS E0466)

criteria.description: Severe COPD with baseline PaCO2 ≥ 52 mm Hg
Sleep apnea considered and ruled out prior to therapy
Cannot be treated with RAD; ventilator will provide AVAPS

required_documentation: Baseline ABG documenting PaCO2 ≥ 52 mm Hg
Documentation ruling out sleep apnea as predominant cause
review_notes: Severe COPD threshold PaCO2 ≥ 52 mm Hg awake on prescribed FIO2.

source_quote: Initial request for the first three months of noninvasive home ventilator use for obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OHS) (also known as Pickwickian syndrome), all of the following: 1. BMI ≥ 30;13,14 2. An initial arterial blood gas PaCO2, done while awake and breathing at baseline and the prescribed FIO2 is ≥ 45 mm Hg;13,14
clinical_service_or_procedure: Noninvasive Home Ventilator - Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome (OHS) (HCPCS E0466)

criteria.description: PSG confirms sleep-disordered hypoventilation without other primary cause

required_documentation: Awake ABG showing PaCO2 ≥ 45 mm Hg
review_notes: OHS requires BMI ≥ 30, awake PaCO2 ≥ 45 mm Hg, and PSG.

source_quote: continued use of noninvasive home ventilators after the initial three-month certification period is medically necessary when meeting the following: A. The device is used for at least an average of four hours per 24-hour period;5 B. Documentation supports both of the following: 1. Ongoing benefits from use of the device;5,10 2. The noninvasive home ventilator is not being used provide RAD or CPAP therapy
clinical_service_or_procedure: Noninvasive Home Ventilator - Continued Use (HCPCS E0466)

criteria.description: Device used for at least average of 4 hours per 24-hour period
Documented ongoing clinical benefit from use
Not being used to provide RAD/CPAP therapy

required_documentation: Device compliance download confirming ≥4 hours/24hr usage
Pulmonologist clinical follow-up documenting ongoing benefit
review_notes: Continuation requires adherence ≥ 4 hours/day and clinical benefit.

source_quote: noninvasive home ventilators for overlap syndromes (presence of more than one condition, such as COPD and sleep apnea) require secondary review by a medical director.4,10
clinical_service_or_procedure: Noninvasive Home Ventilator - Overlap Syndromes (COPD + Sleep Apnea)

criteria.description: Presence of overlap syndrome (COPD + sleep apnea)
Secondary review completed by medical director

review_notes: Mandatory secondary review by medical director for overlap syndromes.

source_quote: initial and ongoing use of an invasive ventilator is medically necessary for a long-term/chronic condition or disease affecting the ability to effectively maintain an adequate respiratory

criteria.description: Long-term/chronic respiratory condition requiring invasive tracheostomy ventilation

required_documentation: Pulmonology records confirming tracheostomy and ventilator dependence
review_notes: Invasive ventilation via tracheostomy indicated for chronic respiratory failure.

source_section: Policy/Criteria - Section V Second / Back-up Ventilator
source_quote: a second or back up noninvasive or invasive ventilator is considered medically necessary for the following indications: A. A second ventilator to serve a different purpose from the first ventilator, based on medical needs.
clinical_service_or_procedure: Second or Back-up Ventilator (HCPCS E0465, E0466)

criteria.description: Serves a different purpose based on medical needs (e.g. negative pressure vs positive pressure)
Wheelchair-mounted during day and bed-mounted at night
Residence in remote area with poor emergency access

required_documentation: Physician clinical documentation justifying second ventilator purpose, wheelchair mount, or remote area
review_notes: Back-up ventilator requires distinct functional justification or geographic isolation.
